newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BP shares jump as market cheers profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BP shares jump as market cheers profit.

text.p: A 16 percent surge in British Petroleum Co Plc's second-quarter profit propelled the oil giant's shares to record levels on Tuesday.
BP also raised its quarterly dividend by five percent over the first quarter, making for a 16 percent rise against a year ago, and proposed share buybacks.
Industry watchers hailed the profit rise as "brilliant" and "extremely pleasing", raised their full-year forecasts and upgraded BP shares.
They also greeted BP plans to buy back shares, although these had been expected to be in the pipeline.

BP's second-quarter net profit rose to 740 million pounds ($1.2 billion) from 648 million last year, while the most optimistic market forecasts had been for 690 million pounds. Underlying first half earnings were up 21 percent to 2.44 billion pounds before exceptional items.
BP said the results were fuelled by higher downstream and chemicals earnings, with volume increases in all areas and further cost savings.
Refining and marketing profits represented the best second-quarter performance in a decade and results in the chemicals sector rose 24 percent.

Upstream, oil and gas production profits were hit by the pound's strength, but they were unchanged in dollar terms with an improved operating performance offsetting the negative impact of a lower oil price.
BP expects higher upstream production in the second half of the year. It sees oil demand staying strong, but added that increasing Iraqi exports "may lead to short term price volatility".

Refining margins fell in July and will likely remain under pressure, but there should be compensating effects both from existing marketing activities and recent entry into new markets, BP said, without giving details.
The European downstream merger with Mobil Corp will lead to significantly extra revenues and cost savings later this year, BP said.
Chemical prices are expected to remain steady in the short term, but they could weaken later as new capacity comes onstream.
BP said it has already achieved its 1997 goal of improving its underlying performance by $300 million through productivity gains and cost savings.
The latest set of results put BP way ahead of other oil majors in terms of return on capital employed, analyst John Toalster at SocGen said.
He put BP's return at 18 percent against 12.5 percent for Shell, 13.2 percent for Mobil, and 15.9 percent for Exxon Corp.
"There is a wide gap now with the other majors," Toalster said. He raised his recommendation for BP to "buy" from "undervalued" as the company's raced 28 pence ahead to 850 before easing to 848.
BP also announced proposed share buybacks, which analysts expect to total between 300 and 500 million pounds next year.
"I believe we can say we have the capacity for additional distribution to shareholders," BP's chief executive John Browne said in a statement.
BP raised its interim dividend by 10 percent to 5.5 per share. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
